learnings.fact: This host's comments sidebar opens ONLY from a TRUSTED click on <velt-sidebar-button>. A JS .click() and a synthetic composed pointer sequence both fail.
learnings.why: The host toggles React state from Velt's own `sidebarButtonClick` event (components/velt/useVeltEventHandlers.ts:63-69). Velt's custom element ignores untrusted events. A fresh page has 0 live [velt-wireframe-id] elements, so any probe run before opening measures nothing and false-concludes.
learnings.evidence: Proven live 2026-07-29: JS .click() on velt-sidebar-button => panel=0; synthetic pointerover/down/up+click (composed:true, aimed via elementFromPoint) => panel=0; Playwright page.mouse.click / locator.click({force:true}) => panel=1, cards=6.

learnings.fact: The sidebar toggle is a TOGGLE, so a bare click drive is not idempotent across blocks sharing one run tab. Prefix the drive with a reload to make it deterministic.
learnings.why: dom-snapshot/measure-block reuse ONE run tab and only resetState() between blocks, which does not close the sidebar. Block 1 opens it; block 2's click closes it. A page reload resets the host's `isGlobalSidebarOpen` React state to false.
learnings.evidence: Drive [eval setTimeout(()=>location.reload(),0)] + sleep 7000 + waitFor velt-sidebar-button + click + waitFor .vc-list-item proved idempotent over 3 consecutive runs from both open and closed preconditions. dom-snapshot went 0/8 -> 7/8 captured.
learnings.statement: The sidebar toggle is a TOGGLE, so a bare click drive is not idempotent across blocks sharing one run tab. Prefix the drive with a reload to make it deterministic.
learnings.context: dom-snapshot/measure-block reuse ONE run tab and only resetState() between blocks, which does not close the sidebar. Block 1 opens it; block 2's click closes it. A page reload resets the host's `isGlobalSidebarOpen` React state to false.

learnings.fact: A wireframe TAG (e.g. velt-comment-dialog-wireframe) is never a valid liveSelector — no element with that tag ever paints. dom-snapshot then reports the misleading error 'surface is occluded'.
learnings.why: dom-snapshot's paintTrue() does `if (!surf) return false`, and the caller renders any false as an occlusion/toggle problem. The real fault is a selector that matches zero painted elements, which sends agents hunting for a non-existent overlay.
learnings.evidence: Diagnosed live: surfFound=false for velt-comment-dialog-wireframe while the content probe hit .vc-head with contained=true (paint was fine). Correcting all 8 liveSelectors to real painted classes (.vc-panel/.vc-focused/.vc-card/...) took dom-snapshot from 0/8 to 7/8.
learnings.statement: A wireframe TAG (e.g. velt-comment-dialog-wireframe) is never a valid liveSelector — no element with that tag ever paints. dom-snapshot then reports the misleading error 'surface is occluded'.
learnings.context: dom-snapshot's paintTrue() does `if (!surf) return false`, and the caller renders any false as an occlusion/toggle problem. The real fault is a selector that matches zero painted elements, which sends agents hunting for a non-existent overlay.

learnings.fact: deltaCompare scores Figma SVG path STROKES as if they were CSS borders, producing false 'border colour' diffs like `1px solid #465169` vs `0px solid rgb(226,232,240)` on every icon.
learnings.why: This is the single largest source of residual delta rows and it is what currently makes a mechanical PASS unreachable on an otherwise-correct build. Acting on the rows would add CSS borders to icons and visibly break them.
learnings.evidence: Recurs on every block of this loop; 5 of the 9 residual rows on state-sidebar-components-sidebar-comment-double-clicked-header are this artifact. The glyphs render correctly at every one of those rows.

learnings.fact: Connecting Playwright to a CDP browser whose DEFAULT CONTEXT was destroyed fails with `Protocol error (Browser.setDownloadBehavior): Browser context management is not supported`, even though /json/version still answers normally.
learnings.why: The process staying alive makes the endpoint look healthy, so agents retry against a permanently broken browser. This is the observable signature of an earlier agent violating the page.close()-only rule. Recovery is to launch a fresh Chrome on a NEW port and re-pin browser-ws.txt — never to reuse the wedged one.
learnings.evidence: Port 9333 answered /json/version with the same WS id as pinned, but every connectOverCDP threw the above. A fresh Chrome on 9334 (own --user-data-dir) connected immediately and ran the whole rest of the phase.
learnings.statement: Connecting Playwright to a CDP browser whose DEFAULT CONTEXT was destroyed fails with `Protocol error (Browser.setDownloadBehavior): Browser context management is not supported`, even though /json/version still answers normally.

learnings.fact: `focusedThreadMode={true}` must accompany `openAnnotationInFocusMode={true}` on <VeltCommentsSidebar> — the latter alone is inert and no thread view ever opens.
learnings.why: This one missing prop gated the entire Loop 2 feature; the app already had the other half, which makes the omission easy to miss on a live read.
learnings.evidence: Added to components/document/document-canvas.tsx; typechecks (so it is a real SDK prop, not an R10 guess) and the focused view then rendered with .vc-focused/.vc-back/.vc-thread-title all live and .vc-panel replaced.

learnings.fact: Card chrome belongs on the per-comment ThreadCard, not on the shared Body wrapper, or a multi-comment thread renders as one continuous shell.
learnings.why: Putting radius/shadow/background on velt-comment-dialog-body-internal looks correct in a sidebar LIST (only one ThreadCard visible per Body) and silently breaks the moment a focused/thread view renders several ThreadCards inside one Body. This was the only demo-breaking defect of the loop.
learnings.evidence: Measured 0px radius / no shadow on all 5 focused cards; after moving the chrome to velt-comment-dialog-thread-card-internal (scoped to .vc-focused-dialog) all 5 measured 12px radius, spec two-layer shadow, white background, 12px gaps, with the list view unregressed.
learnings.statement: Card chrome belongs on the per-comment ThreadCard, not on the shared Body wrapper, or a multi-comment thread renders as one continuous shell.
learnings.context: Putting radius/shadow/background on velt-comment-dialog-body-internal looks correct in a sidebar LIST (only one ThreadCard visible per Body) and silently breaks the moment a focused/thread view renders several ThreadCards inside one Body. This was the only demo-breaking defect of the loop.

learnings.fact: memory.mjs load HIDES tentative entries by default, so cross-phase memory reads as EMPTY even when memory.json is fully populated. Always run `memory.mjs load --include-tentative`.
learnings.why: The auto-promote-at-every-stop flow writes tier=tentative (confirmed only happens on the user saying "phase N complete"). load() defaults includeTentative:false, so every agent told to "load memory first" gets an empty advisory prior and concludes no prior knowledge exists. This defeats the entire point of the auto-promote change, and it is easily misdiagnosed as promote silently dropping entries.
learnings.evidence: Verified 2026-07-29: bare `memory.mjs load` returned corrections:0 gaps:0 naming:0 mappings:0 while .velt-customize/memory.json on disk held 21 corrections, 4 gaps, 3 naming, 2 mappings. `memory.mjs load --include-tentative` returned all of them. memory.mjs:106-109.
learnings.statement: memory.mjs load HIDES tentative entries by default, so cross-phase memory reads as EMPTY even when memory.json is fully populated. Always run `memory.mjs load --include-tentative`.
learnings.context: The auto-promote-at-every-stop flow writes tier=tentative (confirmed only happens on the user saying "phase N complete"). load() defaults includeTentative:false, so every agent told to "load memory first" gets an empty advisory prior and concludes no prior knowledge exists. This defeats the entire point of the auto-promote change, and it is easily misdiagnosed as promote silently dropping entries.

learnings.gap: Resting tall composer (bs-3) — velt-composer-open flips on typed CONTENT, not focus
learnings.why: The design draws the tall attach/@/send composer at rest; the only CSS hook would be :focus-within, which R27 forbids for layout.
learnings.evidence: Reproduced live this loop independently of Loop 1: composer measures 378x40 resting and 378x80 once content is typed. Genuine SDK gap on @veltdev/react 6.0.0-beta.10.
